revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Overtime Hours Limit
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Chen's team can use at most 40 hours of overtime this week to close the case. So far the team has logged 26 hours. Write an inequality for the additional overtime hours t the team can still use, solve it, and graph the solution set on a number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The inequality is 26 + t ≤ 40. Subtracting 26 from both sides: t ≤ 40 − 26 = 14. Since ≤ includes the boundary, graph a closed circle at 14 and shade left (toward smaller values), meaning the team can use 14 or fewer additional overtime hours this week.

launch.narrative: Detective Santos is closing a complex case. She has collected equations and inequalities from different parts of the investigation. One clue says: 'The total value of stolen items divided equally among 4 accomplices gave each person $85.' Another says: 'The lookout earned less than $50.' She must model both clues mathematically and check if the answers are reasonable. Can you help?
launch.contextImage: Detective at a table assembling puzzle pieces, each piece showing an equation or inequality
noticePrompts: Which clue leads to an equation and which leads to an inequality?
What operation does 'divided equally among 4' suggest?
What does 'less than $50' tell you about the inequality symbol?
wonderPrompts: How do you decide when to use an equation versus an inequality?
What would happen if the lookout earned exactly $50 — would the clue still work?

conceptIntro.heading: Should I model this problem with an equation or an inequality?
conceptIntro.intro: To model means to write a real situation as math. I use an equation when there is one exact total, and an inequality when there is a limit or a range of allowed values.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 'Equals' or 'exactly' points to an equation (=); 'at least, at most, more than, fewer than' points to an inequality.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Clue: 'A total divided equally among 4 people gave each $85.'
This has an exact total, so I use an equation. Let t be the total.
Divided among 4 to get 85 means t ÷ 4 = 85, so t = 85 × 4 = 340.
Check reasonableness: $340 split 4 ways is $85 each. That makes sense!

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Clue: 'The lookout earned less than $50.' Equation or inequality?
'Less than' is a limit, so it is an inequality. Let e be the earnings.
'Less than 50' means e < 50. Is $30 a reasonable value? Yes.

explore.instructions: Read each word problem. Decide if it needs an equation or an inequality. Write the mathematical model, solve it, and check your answer for reasonableness.

rows.wordProblem: A detective splits 42 clues equally among 6 case boards. How many clues per board?
rows.reasonable: Yes — 7 clues per board makes sense.

rows.wordProblem: A witness says the suspect carried fewer than 10 items. If the suspect already had 3, how many more could they carry?
rows.reasonable: Yes — up to 6 more items is reasonable.

rows.wordProblem: The evidence room needs at least 50 storage bins. They already have 28. How many more do they need?
rows.reasonable: Yes — at least 22 more bins makes sense.

hints: If the problem uses 'is,' 'equals,' or 'gives exactly,' use an equation (=). If it uses 'at least,' 'at most,' 'more than,' or 'fewer than,' use an inequality.
After solving, ask: Does my answer make sense in the real-world context? Could the number be negative? A fraction of a person?

diagram.intro: Now write the solving steps on paper-style lines — I'll check each one keeps the same solution.

optional.instructions: Room 1: The case board is a mess. Sort each clue into whether it needs an EQUATION (one exact total) or an INEQUALITY (a limit or range).

items.text: The ransom was split equally among 5 suspects, giving each $40.
items.textEs: El rescate se repartió por igual entre 5 sospechosos, y cada uno recibió $40.

items.text: A number of fingerprints plus 9 equals 21.
items.textEs: Un número de huellas más 9 es igual a 21.

items.text: The getaway car held no more than 6 bags of loot.
items.textEs: El carro de escape llevaba no más de 6 bolsas de botín.

items.text: The alarm must stay on for at least 30 minutes.
items.textEs: La alarma debe quedarse encendida por al menos 30 minutos.

items.text: The witness saw fewer than 4 accomplices.
items.textEs: El testigo vio a menos de 4 cómplices.

items.text: Three identical safes hold exactly 75 coins in all.
items.textEs: Tres cajas fuertes idénticas guardan exactamente 75 monedas en total.

optional.hint: Sort by the key operation or concept each item shows.
optional.explanation: Clues that name one exact total need an equation: the ransom split equally among 5 suspects at $40 each, the fingerprints plus 9 equaling 21, and the three identical safes holding exactly 75 coins. Clues with 'no more than', 'at least', or 'fewer than' mark a boundary rather than a single value, so those three need an inequality.
optional.explanationEs: Las pistas que nombran un total exacto necesitan una ecuación: el rescate repartido en partes iguales entre 5 sospechosos a $40 cada uno, las huellas más 9 que dan 21, y las tres cajas fuertes idénticas con exactamente 75 monedas. Las pistas con 'no more than', 'at least' o 'fewer than' marcan un límite en vez de un solo valor, así que esas tres necesitan una desigualdad.
optional.instructionsEs: Sala 1: El tablero del caso es un desorden. Clasifica cada pista según si necesita una ECUACIÓN (un total exacto) o una DESIGUALDAD (un límite o un rango).

optional.stem: Room 2: The vault keypad clue reads, 'A number of stolen coins plus 6 equals 14.' Solve x + 6 = 14 to find the code x.
optional.explanation: Subtract 6 from both sides: x = 14 − 6 = 8. Check: 8 + 6 = 14 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 6 from both sides: x = 14 − 6 = ___.
6 is a number already given in the equation, not the unknown. Undo the +6 to find what x has to be.
Check this one by substituting it back: your value plus 6 has to land exactly on 14.
optional.stemEs: Sala 2: la pista del teclado de la bóveda dice: 'Un número de monedas robadas más 6 es igual a 14'. Resuelve x + 6 = 14 para hallar el código x.
optional.explanationEs: Resta 6 en los dos lados: x = 14 − 6 = 8. Comprueba: 8 + 6 = 14 ✓
hints: An equation is a balance — whatever you do to one side, you do to the other.
The 6 is being added to x, so undo it with the opposite operation, subtraction.
Subtract 6 from both sides so that x stands alone, then work out 14 − 6.
hintsEs: Una ecuación es un equilibrio: lo que le haces a un lado, se lo haces al otro.
Al x se le está sumando 6, así que deshazlo con la operación contraria, la resta.
Resta 6 en los dos lados para que la x quede sola y luego calcula 14 − 6.

optional.stem: Room 3: A sign warns, 'The safe holds at most 20 gold bars.' Which inequality models the number of bars x?
optional.explanation: 'At most 20' means 20 or fewer, so x ≤ 20.
choiceFeedback: That points the wrong way. 'At most 20' means 20 or fewer.
This allows more than 20 bars, but the sign says the safe cannot go past 20. Check which direction “at most” points.
An equals sign says the safe always holds exactly 20. Think about whether fewer bars would break the rule on the sign.
optional.stemEs: Sala 3: un letrero advierte: 'La caja fuerte guarda como máximo 20 barras de oro'. ¿Qué desigualdad representa el número de barras x?
optional.explanationEs: «Como máximo 20» significa 20 o menos, así que x ≤ 20.
hints: Inequality symbols come straight from word clues like “at most”, “no more than”, “at least”, and “more than”.
“At most 20” means the safe can hold 20, or any number below 20, but never more.
Decide first whether the symbol should include 20 itself, then decide which way it points — toward the smaller numbers or the larger ones.
hintsEs: Los símbolos de desigualdad vienen directamente de palabras clave como «como máximo», «no más de», «por lo menos» y «más de».
«Como máximo 20» significa que la caja fuerte puede guardar 20, o cualquier número menor que 20, pero nunca más.
Decide primero si el símbolo debe incluir el 20, y luego decide hacia dónde apunta: hacia los números menores o hacia los mayores.

optional.stem: Room 4: A locked drawer clue reads, 'Five identical evidence boxes weigh 60 pounds in all.' Solve 5w = 60 for each box's weight w.
optional.explanation: Divide both sides by 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 pounds. Check: 5 × 12 = 60 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Divide both sides by 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = ___ pounds.
300 comes from multiplying 5 × 60, but the 60 pounds already includes all five boxes. Multiplication is undone with division.
65 comes from adding 5 and 60, but 5w means 5 times w. Look again at the operation between the 5 and the w.
optional.stemEs: Sala 4: la pista de un cajón cerrado dice: 'Cinco cajas de evidencia idénticas pesan 60 libras en total'. Resuelve 5w = 60 para hallar el peso w de cada caja.
optional.explanationEs: Divide los dos lados entre 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 libras. Comprueba: 5 × 12 = 60 ✓
hints: In 5w, the 5 and the w are multiplied, so undoing it takes the opposite operation.
Divide both sides by 5 so that w is alone on one side.
Set up 60 ÷ 5 to find the weight of a single box, then check by multiplying your answer by 5.
hintsEs: En 5w, el 5 y la w se multiplican, así que deshacerlo requiere la operación contraria.
Divide los dos lados entre 5 para que la w quede sola en un lado.
Plantea 60 ÷ 5 para hallar el peso de una sola caja y después comprueba multiplicando tu respuesta por 5.

optional.label: Room 5: Match each crime-scene clue to the model the detective should write.

pairs.term: The reward divided among 4 detectives gave each $50.
pairs.termEs: La recompensa dividida entre 4 detectives dio $50 a cada uno.

pairs.term: A number of clues take away 7 leaves exactly 9.
pairs.termEs: Un número de pistas menos 7 deja exactamente 9.

pairs.term: The patrol must last more than 8 hours.
pairs.termEs: La patrulla debe durar más de 8 horas.

pairs.term: The locker holds at least 25 files.
pairs.termEs: El casillero guarda al menos 25 expedientes.

optional.hint: Read each item carefully, then match based on what the problem is asking.
optional.explanation: Read the clue words, then choose the symbol. Equal shares and exact totals give equations: the reward split among 4 detectives is 4d = 200, so d = 50, and clues minus 7 leaving 9 is c − 7 = 9, so c = 16. Limits give inequalities with many possible answers: 'more than 8 hours' is h > 8, and 'at least 25 files' is f ≥ 25, where ≥ includes 25 itself.
optional.explanationEs: Lee las palabras clave y luego elige el símbolo. Los repartos iguales y los totales exactos dan ecuaciones: la recompensa repartida entre 4 detectives es 4d = 200, así que d = 50, y las pistas menos 7 que dejan 9 es c − 7 = 9, así que c = 16. Los límites dan desigualdades con muchas respuestas posibles: 'more than 8 hours' es h > 8, y 'at least 25 files' es f ≥ 25, donde ≥ incluye al mismo 25.
optional.labelEs: Sala 5: Une cada pista de la escena del crimen con el modelo que debería escribir el detective.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — The Final Door: Catch the Detective's Mistake

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: Solve the keypad inequality 3x ≤ 18 to find how many bars x fit.
workedExample.workEs: Resuelve la desigualdad del teclado 3x ≤ 18 para saber cuántas barras x caben.

workedExample.label: Step 2
workedExample.work: Divide only the left side by 3: 3x ÷ 3 ≤ 18
workedExample.workEs: Divide solo el lado izquierdo entre 3: 3x ÷ 3 ≤ 18

optional.correctWork: Whatever you do to one side of an inequality, you must do to the OTHER side too. Dividing only the left side by 3 breaks the balance. 3x ≤ 18 becomes 3x ÷ 3 ≤ 18 ÷ 3, which gives x ≤ 6. So at most 6 bars fit, not 18.
hints: The left side was divided by 3, but was the right side divided by 3 too?
Divide BOTH sides by 3: 3x ÷ 3 ≤ 18 ÷ 3, so x ≤ 6.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: la puerta final — atrapa el error del detective
optional.explanation: An inequality stays true only if both sides get exactly the same treatment. Dividing just the left side by 3 breaks that balance, which is how the impossible x ≤ 18 appeared. Dividing both sides gives 3x ÷ 3 ≤ 18 ÷ 3, so x ≤ 6 — at most 6 bars fit.
optional.explanationEs: Una desigualdad sigue siendo verdadera solo si los dos lados reciben exactamente el mismo trato. Dividir solo el lado izquierdo entre 3 rompe ese equilibrio, y así apareció el imposible x ≤ 18. Al dividir ambos lados se obtiene 3x ÷ 3 ≤ 18 ÷ 3, así que x ≤ 6: caben como máximo 6 barras.
optional.correctWorkEs: Lo que hagas a un lado de una desigualdad, debes hacerlo también al OTRO lado. Dividir solo el lado izquierdo entre 3 rompe el equilibrio. 3x ≤ 18 se convierte en 3x ÷ 3 ≤ 18 ÷ 3, lo que da x ≤ 6. Así que caben como máximo 6 barras, no 18.

approaching.stem: A museum has some paintings. After adding 12, they have 45. Which equation models this?
approaching.explanation: 'Adding 12' to the original number gives 45: p + 12 = 45. Solve: p = 33.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Solve: p = ___.
12p means 12 groups of p, which is multiplication. Re-read what actually happened to the paintings the museum already had.
Dividing would split the paintings into 12 equal groups. The museum did something different with the 12.
hints: The museum STARTS with an unknown number of paintings p, then 12 more are ADDED to reach 45.
'Adding 12' means the model joins p and 12 with a plus sign, and the total 45 goes after the equals sign.
Write the story in order: p, plus 12, equals 45. Which choice matches without switching the operation?
approaching.stemEs: Un museo tiene algunas pinturas. Después de agregar 12, tiene 45. ¿Qué ecuación representa esta situación?
approaching.explanationEs: «Agregar 12» al número original da 45: p + 12 = 45. Resuelve: p = 33.
hintsEs: El museo EMPIEZA con un número desconocido de cuadros p y luego se AGREGAN 12 más para llegar a 45.
'Agregar 12' significa que el modelo une p y 12 con un signo más, y el total 45 va después del signo igual.
Escribe la historia en orden: p, más 12, es igual a 45. ¿Qué opción coincide sin cambiar la operación?

approaching.stem: A detective needs more than 8 hours to finish the investigation. She has already worked 3 hours. Which inequality represents the additional hours h she needs?
approaching.explanation: 3 hours plus additional hours h must be more than 8: 3 + h > 8. Solve: h > 5.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Solve: h > 5.
This compares the extra hours to 3, but 3 is the time already worked, not the goal. It is the total of both amounts that has to pass 8.
The 8 and the 3 have swapped jobs here. 8 is the total she must go past, and 3 is what she has already finished.
hints: There are two time pieces: the 3 hours already worked and the extra hours h. Together they must pass 8 hours.
'More than 8' means the TOTAL of 3 + h sits on the big side of a strict inequality — not an equals sign.
Combine first: 3 + h. Then compare that total to 8 using the strict 'more than' symbol. Which choice is built that way?
approaching.stemEs: Una detective necesita más de 8 horas para terminar la investigación. Ya trabajó 3 horas. ¿Qué desigualdad representa las horas adicionales h que necesita?
approaching.explanationEs: 3 horas más las horas adicionales h deben ser más de 8: 3 + h > 8. Resuelve: h > 5.
hintsEs: Hay dos partes de tiempo: las 3 horas ya trabajadas y las horas extra h. Juntas deben pasar de 8 horas.
'Más de 8' significa que el TOTAL de 3 + h queda del lado grande de una desigualdad estricta, no de un signo igual.
Combina primero: 3 + h. Luego compara ese total con 8 usando el símbolo estricto de 'más de'. ¿Qué opción está armada así?

approaching.stem: Which model is correct for: 'A number divided by 6 equals 7'?
approaching.explanation: Divided by 6 is n / 6. Equals 7 means = 7. So n / 6 = 7.
choiceFeedback: "Divided" means division, not multiplication.
That shows subtracting 6. The words say divided by 6.
Use division here, not addition.
hints: Spot the operation phrase: 'divided by 6'. That phrase gives you the symbol between n and 6.
Keep the sentence order — the number n comes first, then the division by 6, then 'equals 7'.
Write n / 6 on the left and 7 on the right. Which choice shows division rather than multiplying or adding 6?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué modelo es correcto para: 'Un número dividido entre 6 es igual a 7'?
approaching.explanationEs: Dividido entre 6 es n / 6. Es igual a 7 significa = 7. Entonces n / 6 = 7.
hintsEs: Identifica la frase de operación: 'dividido entre 6'. Esa frase te da el símbolo entre n y 6.
Conserva el orden de la oración: el número n va primero, luego la división entre 6 y luego 'es igual a 7'.
Escribe n / 6 a la izquierda y 7 a la derecha. ¿Qué opción muestra división en vez de multiplicar o sumar 6?

approaching.stem: A bus can carry at most 48 passengers. There are already 31 on board. Which inequality shows how many more can board?
approaching.explanation: 'At most 48' means the total must be ≤ 48. So 31 + p ≤ 48. Solve: p ≤ 17.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 'At most 48' means the total must be ≤ 48.
An equals sign forces the bus to end up exactly full. Think about whether “at most” also allows a total below the limit.
Subtracting takes away the 31 riders who are already aboard. They belong with the new riders, not apart from them.
hints: The bus already has 31 riders, and p more may board — but the TOTAL cannot pass 48.
'At most 48' allows exactly 48 but nothing above it, so you need the symbol with the 'or equal' bar, not > or =.
Add the parts first: 31 + p. Then cap that sum at 48 with the 'at most' symbol. Which choice matches?
approaching.stemEs: Un autobús puede llevar como máximo 48 pasajeros. Ya hay 31 a bordo. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra cuántos más pueden subir?
approaching.explanationEs: «Como máximo 48» significa que el total debe ser ≤ 48. Entonces 31 + p ≤ 48. Resuelve: p ≤ 17.
hintsEs: El autobús ya lleva 31 pasajeros y pueden subir p más, pero el TOTAL no puede pasar de 48.
'A lo sumo 48' permite exactamente 48 pero nada por encima, así que necesitas el símbolo con la barra de 'o igual', no > ni =.
Suma primero las partes: 31 + p. Luego limita esa suma a 48 con el símbolo de 'a lo sumo'. ¿Qué opción coincide?

approaching.instructions: Sort each word problem into whether it needs an equation or an inequality.

categories.label: Equation (=)
items: Five boxes weigh exactly 60 pounds total. How much does each weigh?
itemsEs: Cinco cajas pesan exactamente 60 libras en total. ¿Cuánto pesa cada una?
Un número más 8 es igual a 20.

categories.label: Inequality (<, >, ≤, ≥)
items: A shelf holds at most 30 books. There are already 17. How many more fit?
The temperature must stay above 32 degrees.
itemsEs: Un estante aguanta a lo más 30 libros. Ya hay 17. ¿Cuántos más caben?
La temperatura debe mantenerse por encima de 32 grados.

hints: 'Exactly,' 'equals,' and 'is' signal an equation.
'At most,' 'at least,' 'above,' 'more than,' and 'fewer than' signal an inequality.
approaching.label: Sort each problem: equation or inequality?
approaching.explanation: Words that pin down one exact value call for an equation: five boxes weighing 'exactly 60 pounds total' and 'a number plus 8 equals 20' each have a single answer. Words that set a limit or a range call for an inequality: a shelf that holds 'at most 30 books' allows 30 or fewer, and a temperature that must stay 'above 32 degrees' allows any value greater than 32.
approaching.explanationEs: Las palabras que fijan un solo valor exacto piden una ecuación: cinco cajas que pesan 'exactly 60 pounds total' y 'a number plus 8 equals 20' tienen cada una una sola respuesta. Las palabras que ponen un límite o un rango piden una desigualdad: un estante que sostiene 'at most 30 books' permite 30 o menos, y una temperatura que debe quedar 'above 32 degrees' permite cualquier valor mayor que 32.
hintsEs: 'Exactamente', 'es igual a' y 'es' señalan una ecuación.
'A lo sumo', 'al menos', 'por encima de', 'más de' y 'menos de' señalan una desigualdad.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: A detective already found 8 fingerprints at the scene. After dusting more surfaces, she has 15 fingerprints in all. How many new fingerprints did she find?
workedExample.workEs: Una detective ya encontró 8 huellas dactilares en la escena. Después de revisar más superficies, tiene 15 huellas en total. ¿Cuántas huellas nuevas encontró?

approaching.correctWork: The variable x is increased by 8, so you undo addition by subtracting 8 from both sides (the inverse operation), not by adding 8 again. x + 8 = 15 becomes x = 15 − 8 = 7. So she found 7 new fingerprints. Check: 7 + 8 = 15 ✓
hints: x is increased by 8. What operation undoes adding 8 — adding 8 again, or subtracting 8?
Subtract 8 from both sides: x = 15 − 8 = 7 new fingerprints.
approaching.explanation: The model x + 8 = 15 is set up correctly, but the solving step adds 8 again instead of undoing it. Since 8 was added to x, you subtract 8 from both sides: x = 15 − 8 = 7 new fingerprints. Check it in the story: 7 + 8 = 15 ✓
approaching.explanationEs: El modelo x + 8 = 15 está bien planteado, pero el paso de resolver vuelve a sumar 8 en lugar de deshacer la suma. Como al x se le sumó 8, hay que restar 8 en ambos lados: x = 15 − 8 = 7 huellas nuevas. Compruébalo en la historia: 7 + 8 = 15 ✓
approaching.correctWorkEs: La variable x está aumentada en 8, así que la suma se deshace restando 8 de ambos lados (la operación inversa), no sumando 8 otra vez. x + 8 = 15 se convierte en x = 15 − 8 = 7. Así que encontró 7 huellas nuevas. Comprueba: 7 + 8 = 15 ✓

rows.wordProblem: Five identical boxes weigh a total of 60 pounds. How much does each box weigh?
rows.reasonable: Yes — 12 pounds per box is reasonable.

rows.wordProblem: A shelf can hold at most 30 books. There are already 17 books. How many more can be added?
rows.reasonable: Yes — up to 13 more books fits.

rows.wordProblem: A baker split 84 cookies equally into bags of 12. How many bags did she use?

onLevel.label: Write a model, solve, and check reasonableness for each problem.
onLevel.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: For each row: find the numbers, decide the operation from the story's clue words, then ask if the answer makes real-world sense.
Equal groups (boxes, bags) point to a multiplication model; 'at most' points to an inequality with the 'or equal' bar. Solve with the inverse operation.
Row 1: five EQUAL boxes total 60 pounds — write a multiplication model with w, then divide both sides by 5. Is that weight per box sensible?
onLevel.explanation: Each row goes story → model → solution → reasonableness check. Five equal boxes totaling 60 pounds is 5w = 60, so w = 12 pounds. 'At most 30 books' with 17 already on the shelf is 17 + b ≤ 30, so b ≤ 13 books. And 84 cookies split into bags of 12 is 12b = 84, so b = 7 bags. Each answer is checked by putting it back into the story: 7 bags of 12 really is 84 cookies.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada fila va de la historia al modelo, luego a la solución y por último a la comprobación de sentido. Cinco cajas iguales que suman 60 libras es 5w = 60, así que w = 12 libras. 'At most 30 books' con 17 ya en el estante es 17 + b ≤ 30, así que b ≤ 13 libros. Y 84 galletas repartidas en bolsas de 12 es 12b = 84, así que b = 7 bolsas. Cada respuesta se comprueba regresándola a la historia: 7 bolsas de 12 sí son 84 galletas.
onLevel.labelEs: Escribe un modelo, resuelve y comprueba que la respuesta sea razonable en cada problema.
hintsEs: En cada fila: halla los números, decide la operación con las palabras clave de la historia y luego pregunta si la respuesta tiene sentido en la vida real.
Los grupos iguales (cajas, bolsas) apuntan a un modelo de multiplicación; 'a lo sumo' apunta a una desigualdad con la barra de 'o igual'. Resuelve con la operación inversa.
Fila 1: cinco cajas IGUALES suman 60 libras; escribe un modelo de multiplicación con w y luego divide ambos lados entre 5. ¿Ese peso por caja tiene sentido?

onLevel.stem: A student solved 4n = 52 and got n = 13. Is the answer reasonable if n represents the number of notebooks in a box?
choices: Yes — 13 notebooks per box is reasonable
Yes — but only if n is a fraction
onLevel.explanation: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 notebooks per box is a reasonable whole number answer.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. notebooks per box is a reasonable whole number answer.
48 comes from subtracting 4 from 52, but 4n means 4 times n. Multiplication is undone with division.
Notebooks are counted in whole numbers, and substituting the solution back into 4n = 52 works out exactly. No fraction is needed here.
hints: 'Reasonable' asks two things: does the math check out, AND does the number make sense for notebooks in a box?
Check the math first: multiply 4 by 13 and see if it rebuilds 52. Then judge whether that count fits a real box of notebooks.
Compute 4 × 13. Does it equal 52? Then ask: could a box realistically hold that many notebooks? Match your reasoning to one choice.
onLevel.stemEs: Un estudiante resolvió 4n = 52 y obtuvo n = 13. ¿Es razonable la respuesta si n representa el número de cuadernos en una caja?
onLevel.explanationEs: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 cuadernos por caja es una respuesta razonable con un número entero.
choicesEs: Sí — 13 cuadernos por caja es razonable
Sí — pero solo si n es una fracción
hintsEs: 'Razonable' pregunta dos cosas: ¿cuadran las cuentas Y tiene sentido ese número de cuadernos en una caja?
Revisa primero las cuentas: multiplica 4 por 13 y ve si reconstruye 52. Luego juzga si esa cantidad cabe en una caja real de cuadernos.
Calcula 4 × 13. ¿Da 52? Luego pregunta: ¿podría una caja tener realmente esa cantidad de cuadernos? Une tu razonamiento con una opción.

onLevel.label: Match each situation to its correct model

pairs.situation: A recipe needs exactly 3 cups of flour.
You must read more than 20 pages tonight.
Each team has the same number of players, and there are 36 players on 4 teams.
The pool temperature must be at least 72°F.

onLevel.hint: Read each item carefully, then match based on what the problem is asking.
hints: Sort by clue words first: 'exactly' and 'the same number' pin down ONE value; 'more than' and 'at least' allow many values.
One-value clues get an equation with =. Range clues get an inequality. Then confirm with the numbers: 3 cups, 20 pages, 36 players, 72°F.
Start with the recipe: 'exactly 3 cups' is one fixed amount, so find the model with an equals sign and the number 3.
onLevel.explanation: The clue words decide the symbol. 'Exactly 3 cups' fixes one value, so f = 3, and 4 equal teams holding 36 players is 4t = 36 — both are equations with a single answer. 'More than 20 pages' and 'at least 72°F' each allow a whole range of values, so they need inequalities: p > 20 and t ≥ 72, where ≥ includes 72 itself.
onLevel.explanationEs: Las palabras clave deciden el símbolo. 'Exactly 3 cups' fija un solo valor, así que f = 3, y 4 equipos iguales con 36 jugadores es 4t = 36; las dos son ecuaciones con una sola respuesta. 'More than 20 pages' y 'at least 72°F' permiten todo un rango de valores, así que necesitan desigualdades: p > 20 y t ≥ 72, donde ≥ incluye al mismo 72.
onLevel.labelEs: Empareja cada situación con su modelo correcto

onLevel.label: Solve this two-step problem: 3x + 5 = 26
hints: First subtract 5 from both sides: 3x = 21.
Then divide both sides by 3: x = 7. Check: 3(7) + 5 = 21 + 5 = 26 ✓
onLevel.explanation: Undo the operations in reverse order. First take away the 5 that was added: 3x + 5 − 5 = 26 − 5, so 3x = 21. Then undo the multiplication by dividing both sides by 3: x = 7. Check: 3(7) + 5 = 21 + 5 = 26 ✓
onLevel.explanationEs: Deshaz las operaciones en orden inverso. Primero quita el 5 que se sumó: 3x + 5 − 5 = 26 − 5, así que 3x = 21. Después deshaz la multiplicación dividiendo ambos lados entre 3: x = 7. Comprueba: 3(7) + 5 = 21 + 5 = 26 ✓

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Seven evidence lockers hold 84 case files in all, split equally. How many files per locker?
workedExample.workEs: Siete casilleros de evidencia guardan 84 expedientes en total, repartidos por igual. ¿Cuántos expedientes por casillero?

onLevel.correctWork: The variable f is multiplied by 7, so you undo it by dividing both sides by 7 (the inverse operation), not by subtracting 7. 7f = 84 becomes f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12. So there are 12 files per locker. Check: 7 × 12 = 84 ✓
hints: f is multiplied by 7. What operation undoes multiplying by 7 — subtracting 7 or dividing by 7?
Divide both sides by 7: f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 files per locker.
onLevel.explanation: The model 7f = 84 is correct, but f is MULTIPLIED by 7, and subtracting 7 does not undo a multiplication. Divide both sides by 7 instead: f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 files per locker. Check: 7 × 12 = 84 ✓
onLevel.explanationEs: El modelo 7f = 84 está correcto, pero la f está MULTIPLICADA por 7, y restar 7 no deshace una multiplicación. Hay que dividir ambos lados entre 7: f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 archivos por casillero. Comprueba: 7 × 12 = 84 ✓
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La variable f está multiplicada por 7, así que se deshace dividiendo ambos lados entre 7 (la operación inversa), no restando 7. 7f = 84 se convierte en f = 84 ÷ 7 = 12. Así que hay 12 expedientes por casillero. Comprueba: 7 × 12 = 84 ✓

extending.title: Find the Problem-Solving Error

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: A parking lot holds at most 200 cars. There are 134 already. How many more can park?
workedExample.workEs: Un estacionamiento admite como máximo 200 autos. Ya hay 134. ¿Cuántos más pueden estacionarse?

extending.correctWork: 'At most' means less than or equal to, so the model should be an inequality: 134 + c ≤ 200. Solving: c ≤ 66. Up to 66 more cars can park, not exactly 66.
hints: The problem says 'at most 200.' Does that mean exactly 200 or up to 200?
'At most' requires ≤, not =. The correct model is 134 + c ≤ 200, so c ≤ 66.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error al resolver el problema
extending.explanation: The arithmetic is fine, but the model is too strict. 'At most 200 cars' means the lot can hold 200 or fewer, which is ≤, not =. The model should be 134 + c ≤ 200, giving c ≤ 66 — up to 66 more cars can park, not exactly 66.
extending.explanationEs: Las cuentas están bien, pero el modelo es demasiado estricto. 'At most 200 cars' significa que el estacionamiento puede tener 200 o menos, y eso es ≤, no =. El modelo debe ser 134 + c ≤ 200, lo que da c ≤ 66: pueden estacionarse hasta 66 autos más, no exactamente 66.
extending.correctWorkEs: 'Como máximo' significa menor o igual que, así que el modelo debe ser una desigualdad: 134 + c ≤ 200. Al resolver: c ≤ 66. Hasta 66 autos más pueden estacionarse, no exactamente 66.

extending.prompt: Create two word problems about the same situation: one that requires an equation and one that requires an inequality. Solve both and explain why the models are different.
extending.sentenceFrame: Equation problem: ___. Model: ___. Solution: ___. Inequality problem: ___. Model: ___. Solution: ___. The models are different because ___.
extending.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: Use the same situation twice: one question asks for an EXACT amount, the other sets a limit or a minimum.
Choose clue words on purpose: 'exactly' or 'in total' for your equation; 'at least', 'at most', or 'more than' for your inequality.
Pick a scene, like saving money. Write 'I saved exactly $__' for the equation, then 'I need at least $__' for the inequality. Solve both and compare.
extending.explanation: The two models differ because the two questions ask for different things. An equation fits when the situation names one exact amount, like 'I saved exactly $45', so it has a single solution. An inequality fits when the situation sets a minimum or a ceiling, like 'I need at least $45', so a whole range of values works. Same story, different clue words, different symbol.
extending.explanationEs: Los dos modelos son distintos porque las dos preguntas piden cosas distintas. Una ecuación sirve cuando la situación nombra una cantidad exacta, como 'ahorré exactamente $45', así que tiene una sola solución. Una desigualdad sirve cuando la situación pone un mínimo o un tope, como 'necesito al menos $45', así que funciona todo un rango de valores. La misma historia, distintas palabras clave, distinto símbolo.
extending.promptEs: Crea dos problemas sobre la misma situación: uno que requiera una ecuación y otro que requiera una desigualdad. Resuelve los dos y explica por qué los modelos son diferentes.
hintsEs: Usa la misma situación dos veces: una pregunta pide una cantidad EXACTA y la otra fija un límite o un mínimo.
Escoge las palabras clave a propósito: 'exactamente' o 'en total' para tu ecuación; 'al menos', 'a lo sumo' o 'más de' para tu desigualdad.
Escoge una escena, como ahorrar dinero. Escribe 'Ahorré exactamente $__' para la ecuación y luego 'Necesito al menos $__' para la desigualdad. Resuelve ambas y compara.

rows.problem: A tank holds at most 500 gallons. It has 320. How many more gallons can be added?
Six friends split a pizza bill equally. Each paid $8. What was the total?
A runner must complete more than 5 laps. She has done 2. How many more does she need?

extending.label: Check each student's model. If wrong, write the correct model and solve.
extending.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: For each row, compare the problem's clue words to the student's symbol: does 'at most' or 'more than' really match an equals sign?
'At most' calls for ≤ and 'more than' calls for >. An equals sign only fits when the answer is one exact value.
Row 1: the tank holds AT MOST 500, but the student's model uses =. Decide whether that symbol fits the story; if not, rewrite with the limit symbol and solve.
extending.explanation: Row 1 is wrong: 'at most 500 gallons' is a ceiling, so the model needs 320 + g ≤ 500, which gives g ≤ 180. Row 2 is correct: six friends each paying $8 out of one shared total is t / 6 = 8, so t = 48. Row 3 is wrong: 'more than 5 laps' needs a strict >, so 2 + m > 5, giving m > 3.
extending.explanationEs: La fila 1 está mal: 'at most 500 gallons' es un tope, así que el modelo necesita 320 + g ≤ 500, lo que da g ≤ 180. La fila 2 está bien: seis amigos que pagan $8 cada uno de un total compartido es t / 6 = 8, así que t = 48. La fila 3 está mal: 'more than 5 laps' necesita un > estricto, así que 2 + m > 5, lo que da m > 3.
extending.labelEs: Revisa el modelo de cada estudiante. Si está mal, escribe el modelo correcto y resuelve.
hintsEs: En cada fila, compara las palabras clave del problema con el símbolo del estudiante: ¿de verdad 'a lo sumo' o 'más de' corresponden a un signo igual?
'A lo sumo' pide ≤ y 'más de' pide >. Un signo igual solo cuadra cuando la respuesta es un valor exacto.
Fila 1: el tanque contiene A LO SUMO 500, pero el modelo del estudiante usa =. Decide si ese símbolo cuadra con la historia; si no, reescríbelo con el símbolo del límite y resuelve.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving is matching the wrong model to a key phrase. For 'the getaway car held no more than 6 bags,' students often write the equation b = 6 instead of the inequality b ≤ 6, because they see one number and assume it must be exact. The same mistake happens in reverse: for 'the reward split equally among 5 people gave each $40,' students sometimes write the inequality 5p ≥ 40 instead of the equation 5p = 40, because 'split equally' sounds like it could mean a range. Before you submit, ask: does this phrase give one exact value (equation, =) or a limit/range (inequality, <, >, ≤, ≥)?

diagram.title: Detective's Budget Limit
diagram.caption: She has spent $320 of her $500 cap (closed dot = allowed), so the gap up to $500 shows r ≤ 180 — at most $180 more.

connect.scenario: A detective has a $500 budget for equipment. She has already spent $320. The inequality 320 + r ≤ 500 represents the remaining amount r she can spend. She also needs exactly 4 flashlights at $15 each, represented by the equation 4f = 60.
connect.promptQuestion: How much more can the detective spend? How much does each flashlight cost? When do you use an equation versus an inequality?
connect.prompt: The detective can spend at most $__ more because r ≤ 500 − ___ = ___. Each flashlight costs $__ because f = 60 ÷ ___ = ___.

check.explanation: Subtract 320 from both sides: r ≤ 500 − 320 = 180. She can spend at most $180 more.
Divide both sides by 4: f = 60 ÷ 4 = $15 per flashlight.

check.stem: Why is one an equation and the other an inequality?
choices: The flashlights cost exactly $60, but the budget is a limit she must stay under
Because equations are for money and inequalities are for counting
check.explanation: 'Exactly' points to one value, so it is an equation. A budget — 'at most' — allows a whole range of values, so it is an inequality.

connect.modelAnswer: Budget: 320 + r ≤ 500, so r ≤ 180 — she can spend at most $180 more. Flashlights: 4f = 60, so f = $15 each. The budget is an inequality because any amount up to $180 is allowed; the flashlight cost is an equation because there is exactly one answer.

exitTicket.stem: A box of donuts has some donuts. After giving away 7, there are fewer than 5 left. Which inequality represents the starting number of donuts d?
exitTicket.explanation: Starting with d donuts and giving away 7 leaves fewer than 5: d − 7 < 5. Solve: d < 12. ✓
choiceFeedback: She gave donuts away, so subtract 7, don't add it.
'Fewer than 5' means less than 5 — use '<', not '>'.
'Fewer than' is an inequality, not equal — use '<'.
hints: Track the story: start with d donuts, GIVE AWAY 7, and what remains is FEWER than 5.
'Giving away' means subtracting from d, and 'fewer than 5' means the strict less-than symbol — not equals and not greater-than.
Build it in story order: d, minus 7, then compare what's left to 5 using '<'. Which choice matches that structure?
